notes: SHARED QUESTION G (rows 1985-SR-IV.4.3.8.4.3-1 and 1985-SR-VI.6.25.3-2): is a group item 'a data item whose usage is DISPLAY' / 'described implicitly or explicitly as USAGE IS DISPLAY' in 1985, even when its own entry writes USAGE COMP? ANSWER: yes. The 1985 text as amended (Amendment 2, 1993) itself treats a group as meeting that test: the class condition requires identifier-1 to be 'a data item whose usage is explicitly or implicitly DISPLAY' and in the same paragraph gives the result for identifier-1 being 'a zero-length group item', which is possible only if a group passes the usage test. A group's class is alphanumeric at object time whatever its subordinates (IV.4.3.3), and a USAGE clause written on a group 'applies to each elementary item in the group' (VI.5.14.4 GR1), so it describes the elementary items, not the group. The next edition says so outright (§2002:8.5.2, kept as §2023:8.5.2.1). Where 1985 is unclear, CLAUDE.md rule 1 lets the ISO text decide, and the ISO text admits the group. Applied here: neither agent could break the elementary half, in which every non-DISPLAY elementary item is refused with COBOL1647. A group, including '01 GC USAGE COMP', is admitted as a DISPLAY item, which is the answer above. ATTACK SURFACE: the verdict depends on reading the 1993 class-condition sentence as evidence that a group satisfies a usage-DISPLAY test, and on the ISO text deciding where 1985 is unclear. A literal reader could say a group whose own entry writes USAGE COMP is 'explicitly' COMP.

next.reason: 1985: "Data-name-1 must reference a data item whose usage is DISPLAY."; 2023: "— a boolean data item, — a national data item, … that is not subordinate to a strongly-typed group item". 1985 allows only usage DISPLAY items. 2023 adds boolean and national items, and refuses some display items: those under strongly-typed groups, and strongly-typed or variable-length groups.
